title: Fictional holdout — how could we use the community room without making promises for one another?

voices.name: Joan
voices.text: I can open the community room every Saturday morning. I have the key and I know how the heating works. We could start with people bringing things they want repaired, rather than buying a lot of equipment. I would enjoy doing something practical with neighbours. I used to help at a repair session and people brought all sorts of things, sometimes just to ask whether they were worth keeping. I need to correct what I said about Saturdays. I have checked the new shift rota and I am working most weekends now. I can open the first session, but I cannot offer a weekly commitment or take responsibility for finding somebody to replace me. Please don't advertise weekly opening on the strength of my first offer.

voices.name: Emil
voices.text: I want this room to be used. At the moment I mostly see notices telling us what we cannot do in it. People have asked me whether I would help because I live nearby. Living nearby does not mean I am free during the day. I could translate a short invitation, but I cannot attend Saturday mornings. That doesn't make me against the repair sessions. I am happy for the invitation to say I helped with the translation. I have not agreed that it can list me as an organiser or as someone responsible for the equipment. If we are asking the council to keep paying for the room, I support that. I do not support telling the council that residents will take over its maintenance. Those are different commitments.

voices.name: Saira
voices.text: You can put my name on the letter asking for longer opening hours. I want the room available in the evening as well as on Saturdays. My daughter and I went to look at it last week. The noticeboard was full of activities we had never heard about, and we could not tell which ones were still happening. A paper notice through the door would reach us better than another chat group. I have now read the draft letter. It also promises that we will collect fees from everyone using the room. I didn't agree to that. I am withdrawing permission to use my name on this version. I still want longer opening hours. Please send me the changed wording before saying I support a new letter.

voices.name: Tom
voices.text: The council has someone paid to look after the building, and I want us to ask what their job covers before we start doing it ourselves. I can make that enquiry and bring back the answer. I cannot promise what the council will say. I also want to know whether the entrance ramp will be fixed. Last time I could not get through the door independently. If the only plan is for neighbours to lift my chair, that is not access I can rely on. I would help choose tools for a repair session once I can get into the room. I don't need somebody else to decide what I can contribute. Ask me directly, and let me tell you what would make it possible.
